nodes.title: Networking fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Networking moves packets between machines using layered protocols (the OSI / TCP-IP stack). Most exam questions test routing decisions, subnetting math, the difference between L2 and L3, and how DNS / DHCP make the whole thing usable for humans.

flashcards.front: What's the difference between Layer 2 and Layer 3?
flashcards.back: L2 (data link) uses MAC addresses to deliver frames inside a single broadcast domain (a switch). L3 (network) uses IP addresses to route packets between networks (a router). Switches do L2; routers do L3.

flashcards.front: How does a subnet mask work?
flashcards.back: The mask splits an IP into a network portion (the high bits, set to 1) and a host portion (the low bits, set to 0). `/24` means the first 24 bits are network = up to 256 hosts (254 usable). `/30` is 4 IPs = 2 hosts — typical for a point-to-point link.

Domain Name System translates human-readable names (`example.com`) into IP addresses. A recursive resolver asks the root, the TLD server (`.com`), and finally the authoritative server for the domain. TTL controls how long answers are cached.

flashcards.front: TCP vs UDP — when do you pick each?
flashcards.back: TCP is reliable, ordered, congestion-controlled — use it when every byte matters (HTTP, SSH, SMTP). UDP is lightweight, no handshake, no retransmit — use it for streaming, gaming, DNS queries, anywhere latency beats reliability.

pairs.stem: A logistics Pub/Sub topic receives shipment events. The WMS and customer notification service must each process ALL shipment events independently. The WMS is currently backlogged. How should you design this?
pairs.option: Create two separate pull subscriptions on the same topic so each service maintains its own independent backlog

pairs.stem: A mobile game needs a database that auto-scales with user load, supports real-time synchronization to mobile clients, and handles offline data access with conflict resolution. Which GCP database is the best fit?
pairs.option: Firestore in Native mode,.

pairs.stem: A media company serves video globally and needs to terminate TLS as close to users as possible while routing to the nearest healthy backend. Which solution achieves this with minimal latency?
pairs.option: Deploy Traffic Director with Envoy proxies in each region for intelligent request routing

pairs.stem: A genomics company stores 100TB/month of raw sequencing data. Data must be immediately accessible for 30 days, retrievable within 1 hour for 1 year, and archived long-term thereafter. Which lifecycle policy minimizes cost?
pairs.option: Standard → Coldline after 30 days → Archive after 365 days

pairs.stem: An IoT platform ingests from 1 million devices. Analytics, alerting, and archival services must each independently process every message without coupling the producer to consumers. What is the correct pattern?
pairs.option: Deploy a central Cloud Function that receives IoT data and directly calls each downstream service API

pairs.stem: A data science team runs daily batch ML feature engineering jobs on 200GB datasets in Cloud Storage. Jobs take 2 hours and run once per day. Which compute approach minimizes costs?
pairs.option: Create an ephemeral Dataproc cluster via workflow templates, run the job,.

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

pairs.stem: A production e-commerce app on GKE experienced downtime when all nodes were in us-central1-a during a zone outage. What configuration prevents single-zone failure?
pairs.option: Create a regional GKE cluster distributing nodes across us-central1-a/b/c with pod anti-affinity rules spreading replicas across zones

pairs.stem: A retail website faces a DDoS attack with 10Gbps L3/L4 traffic and periodic L7 SQLi attempts. What Cloud Armor configuration protects against both attack types?
pairs.option: Use Cloud Armor with a throttling policy to limit all requests exceeding 1,000 RPS from any single IP

pairs.stem: A containerized app on GKE reads from Cloud Storage and writes to BigQuery. Currently a service account key file is mounted as a Kubernetes secret. What is the recommended replacement?
pairs.option: Rotate the service account key every 24 hours using a Cloud Function and update the Kubernetes secret automatically

pairs.stem: A startup wants Kubernetes for containerized microservices without managing node pools, worker nodes, or cluster upgrades. They want to pay only for actual pod resource requests. Which GKE mode is best?
pairs.option: GKE Autopilot, which fully manages node infrastructure and charges only for CPU/memory/storage requested by pods

pairs.stem: A company manages GCP resources using IaC and wants version-controlled, repeatable deployments using only native GCP capabilities without third-party tools. Which GCP-native IaC option should they use?
pairs.option: Cloud Deployment Manager using YAML/Jinja2 or Python templates to define and deploy GCP resources declaratively

pairs.stem: A genomics team runs 8-12 hour ML training jobs and wants to use preemptible resources to minimize costs without losing training progress on preemption. What approach is correct?
pairs.option: Use Spot VMs with automatic restart enabled and accept the job restarting from the beginning

pairs.stem: A Django application backed by Cloud SQL PostgreSQL has read bottlenecks with a 90% read / 10% write ratio. What is the most operationally simple approach to scale reads?
pairs.option: Create Cloud SQL read replicas and configure the application to route SELECT queries to replicas and writes to the primary

pairs.stem: A CISO needs a unified view of security findings, misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and compliance posture across all GCP projects in the organization. What service provides this?
pairs.option: Configure BigQuery log sinks from all projects and build custom queries to detect security findings

pairs.stem: A retailer has 50 stable n2-standard-8 VMs running 24/7 for their catalog service, plus 200 additional VMs needed only during the 3-month holiday season. How should they optimize compute costs?
pairs.option: Buy 3-year Committed Use Discounts for all 250 VMs to maximize discount regardless of seasonal variation

pairs.stem: A microservices application stores secrets across environment variables, Kubernetes secrets, and config files. The security team needs centralized storage, automatic rotation, and audit logging for all secrets. What should you implement?
pairs.option: Migrate all secrets to Secret Manager.

pairs.stem: A media streaming company serves 4K video globally. They need edge caching, DDoS protection, and routing to the nearest healthy origin. Which Google Cloud architecture achieves all three?
pairs.option: Global External HTTPS Load Balancer with Cloud CDN enabled on the backend bucket for edge caching.

pairs.stem: An analytics company has unpredictable ad-hoc analyst queries and predictable overnight ETL batch jobs in BigQuery. How should they optimize costs?
pairs.option: Use on-demand pricing for all queries since it is always cheaper than reservations for mixed workloads

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A team wants a CI pipeline that builds a Docker image, runs unit tests, scans for vulnerabilities, and pushes a signed image to Artifact Registry, triggered on every Git commit. What is the GCP-native implementation?
flashcards.back: Cloud Build is the GCP-native CI service. cloudbuild.yaml defines sequential steps: docker build, run tests, gcloud artifacts docker images scan, then sign the image. Cloud Build triggers fire automatically on repository events (push, PR). Cloud Build has native integration with Artifact Registry, Container Analysis, and Binary Authorization. test, scan, and sign steps; create a Cloud Build trigger linked to the source repository for automatic execution on commit

flashcards.front: A platform team manages GCP policies and Kubernetes configurations across 15 GKE clusters. They want a single Git repository as the source of truth with configurations automatically applied to all clusters. What capability enables this?
flashcards.back: Anthos Config Management (ACM) Config Sync: each cluster runs a Config Sync agent that continuously watches the Git repository. Any change to the repo is automatically applied to all registered clusters within seconds. Supports hierarchical configuration (root sync + namespace-level repo syncs). This is the GCP-native GitOps solution for multi-cluster management. which continuously reconciles cluster state from a Git repository supporting namespace and cluster-scoped configurations

flashcards.front: A GKE deployment was updated with a new container image that immediately started crashing. It has been failing for 5 minutes and must be rolled back to the last working version immediately. What is the fastest solution?
flashcards.back: kubectl rollout undo immediately restores the previous ReplicaSet (Kubernetes keeps rollout history). No Git commit, no CI/CD pipeline wait required. Kubernetes starts the old pods while terminating the new broken pods. This is the fastest recovery path. kubectl delete (option B) causes downtime during the gap between delete and re-apply.

flashcards.front: A developer needs to run a video transcoding job requiring 32GB RAM and up to 75 minutes to complete, triggered by Pub/Sub when new video files arrive in Cloud Storage. Which compute option supports these requirements?
flashcards.back: Cloud Run supports up to 32GB memory and 60-minute request timeout per request (as of 2024). Configure a Pub/Sub push subscription targeting the Cloud Run URL; each message triggers a transcoding job. Cloud Functions 2nd gen has a maximum 60-minute timeout but supports 32GB RAM. However, Cloud Run is the preferred choice for CPU-intensive, long-running container workloads. configure a Pub/Sub push subscription to trigger the Cloud Run service

pairs.stem: A team wants a CI pipeline that builds a Docker image, runs unit tests, scans for vulnerabilities, and pushes a signed image to Artifact Registry, triggered on every Git commit. What is the GCP-native implementation?
pairs.option: Define a cloudbuild.yaml with sequential build.

pairs.stem: A GKE deployment was updated with a new container image that immediately started crashing. It has been failing for 5 minutes and must be rolled back to the last working version immediately. What is the fastest solution?
pairs.option: Run kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> which immediately rolls back to the previous ReplicaSet without Git or CI/CD

pairs.stem: A company wants to validate that their Cloud SQL multi-region setup actually performs failover correctly during zone outages. The SRE team wants to proactively test this in production during low-traffic periods. What is the chaos engineering approach?
pairs.option: Wait for a real zone outage and use the post-incident review to identify failover gaps

pairs.stem: A developer needs to run a video transcoding job requiring 32GB RAM and up to 75 minutes to complete, triggered by Pub/Sub when new video files arrive in Cloud Storage. Which compute option supports these requirements?
pairs.option: App Engine Flexible Environment with a custom runtime configured for 32GB RAM instances

pairs.stem: A platform team manages GCP policies and Kubernetes configurations across 15 GKE clusters. They want a single Git repository as the source of truth with configurations automatically applied to all clusters. What capability enables this?
pairs.option: Deploy Anthos Config Management with Config Sync.

pairs.stem: A company's Cloud Logging costs are too high due to high-volume DEBUG logs from a verbose web server. Developers still need access to these logs but they don't need to be retained in Cloud Logging. What is the correct approach to reduce ingestion costs?
pairs.option: Disable all logging for the web server project and redirect logs to a Cloud Storage bucket via a sink
